name: AIHOT
use_label: Build your own industry news site
one_liner: A site framework that gathers news and writes a daily digest by itself — swap in your sources and standards to make it your industry's hot-topics site.

text.why: Only people inside an industry — law, HR, finance — know which news matters. The author runs the AI hot-topics site aihot.news and open-sourced all of it: the site, back office, selection pipeline, prompts and pass thresholds, so anyone can retarget it to their own field.
text.take: It publishes the selection standards and the prompts themselves, so how items are chosen is fully visible.
build: It collects from RSS, web pages, APIs, X and official accounts, keeps one copy of each item, pre-screens with a large language model, then scores twice independently and keeps only what clears the bar. It writes titles and summaries in Chinese, clusters reports of the same event, and publishes a daily digest at 08:00 plus weekly and monthly reports. You change behaviour by editing the prompts in industry/prompts/.

who.role: People who want to run a news-digest site for their own industry.

start.text: Follow the README's run guide to start the repository, then change the sources and prompts to fit your industry.

caveat: Docs and the site are Chinese-first (the README is in Chinese). It relies on a large language model, so you must arrange model access and cost yourself; which model and what cost could not be confirmed here.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: AIHOT's pipeline diagram: collect, pre-screen, double scoring, write, cluster and publish, in six steps.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
